failures.criterion: Acceptance 1/3/4 (product defect): a child of a closed tree re-admitted as a root of its own keeps its Sandbox, its volume and its roles' sessions — the fit rule now relabels the suspended Sandbox instead of replacing it — while the orphan sweep runs
failures.evidence: Red test TestAnIssueSandboxReadmittedSinceItsDeleteWasDecidedStays in packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/lifecycle_test.go (commit a1b66e68). `cd packages/daemon && CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=1 -run TestAnIssueSandboxReadmittedSinceItsDeleteWasDecidedStays ./internal/runtime/sandbox/` -> `--- FAIL ... the re-admitted issue's Sandbox after the sweep that decided on the old tree's Sandbox = <nil>; want the relabelled Sandbox uid-sandbox-old-tree kept Running under tree LEGION-209, its volume and sessions with it`. Cause: sweep (sandbox.go:810-834) takes issue and tree from the informer snapshot, re-reads only TreeLive(old tree) under the pod turn, and deletes with Preconditions{UID} alone (sandbox.go:831); relaunch.go:269-277 now keeps a suspended Sandbox of another tree and JSON-patches its tree label with the UID unchanged, so a re-admission that lands between the sweep's snapshot and its lockPod is not fenced out: the re-admitted issue's running Sandbox is deleted and background GC takes its PVC (clone, workspace, every role's session); the issue's next launch then runs workspace-init with LEGION_EXPECT_ISSUE_VOLUME=true on an empty volume and exits 3. Before this change the retree replaced the Sandbox (new UID) and the stale fence refused. The controller branch (sandbox.go:803-805), Release (sandbox.go:690) and cleanup.go:70-72 all fence {UID, ResourceVersion}. Fencing the issue-pod delete on {UID, ResourceVersion} (the relabel patch bumps the version) makes the red test, TestTheOrphanSweepDeletesOnlySandboxesOfClosedTreesPastTheGrace and TestALaunchBegunDuringAnOrphansDeleteWaitsForIt pass together (checked in a throwaway edit of sandbox.go:831, reverted). The comment at sandbox.go:731-733, 'an issue Sandbox's tree is read again under the turn', is false today and should state what the code does once fixed.

failures.criterion: Acceptance 3 live proof (proof defect): stage 4b child-release's wait for the done child's Sandbox and PVC to be gone fails closed
failures.evidence: scripts/e2e/stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:2416 `child1_released() { [ -z "$(op get sandboxes,pvc -l ... -o name)" ]; }`: `[ -z "$(...)" ]` discards kubectl's exit status and until_true (scripts/e2e/lib/rig.sh:28) swallows its stderr, so one transient read failure (API 5xx, throttling, the 300 s `op` timeout in scripts/e2e/lib/namespace-rig.sh:28) during the up-to-600 s poll returns true at once. Shell repro: `op() { echo error >&2; return 1; }; child1_released() { [ -z "$(op get x -o name)" ]; }; child1_released && echo PASSES-ON-A-FAILED-READ` prints PASSES-ON-A-FAILED-READ. The `released` log count at 2424-2425 fences the Sandbox half (the daemon logs the release after its foreground delete returned, issue_suspend.go:96), so the exposure is the PVC half of the note at 2431 and a false FAIL that costs the operator a multi-hour rerun; every other 'gone' wait in the script guards the read (`out=$(...) && [ -z "$out" ]` at 573-574, 3634-3635, 3694-3695). The same unguarded pattern re-asserts child 1 at 2905 (`[ -z "$(issue_sandbox_modes ...)" ]`) and 2910 (`[ -z "$(issue_pvcs ...)" ]`). Fix before the operator's stage 4b run, which has not started.

Only the unit golden locks it (manifest_test.go TestEveryContainerOfEveryPodIsGuaranteed over testdata/golden/probe.json), and a unit test is a regression lock, not proof; the plan's gap analysis named the probe pod as the one that would otherwise break 'every Legion pod is Guaranteed'. Wording to fix in this round or the Fast-follow line: packages/daemon/internal/workspace/gitworktree.go:246-250 argues a safety property from 'workspace-init's own per-repository flock', which this change deleted (the argument still holds — no two pods share a clone and tmux provisioning is sequential — but the premise is gone); packages/daemon/internal/workspace/config.go:85 still says 'A tree volume's init containers serialize on the file beside the clone'; docs/solutions/infra/a-sandbox-tree-needs-a-node-that-fits-it.md:55-59 still prescribes the deleted pod anti-affinity as the remedy.

Non-blocking gaps for the implementer's judgement: workflow/close_test.go's child-leave table has no icebox row though the spec names it (linger.go:38-40 branches on done alone, so it provably takes backlog's path); stage 4b sets `record=$work/sandboxes` but never writes it, so namespace-rig's by-name teardown is inert there (label teardown plus namespace_clean still fail the run loudly on a leak); store.IssueSuspension's release wait tests `state <> 'retired'` where the delete's real precondition is IssueHasSessions false (`session_file`) — unreachable today since every stored claim has a machine at boot; sandbox.configure never checks Options.Resources covers every role (DefaultResources fills all seven, so unreachable from a daemon-built Options); ensureSandbox's no-volume replacement loop retries a delete conflict without a sleep (dead after the census).

By design, not a regression: a tree closed at linger expiry keeps every claim's session_file while its cleanup releases the volumes, so re-admitting one of its issues takes the lost-volume relaunch (workspace-init exit 3, `volume was lost` once, a fresh session with workspace-recovered.json) — stage 4b's re-admission checkpoint asserts exactly that; the done child's own close drops the sessions first, so it re-enters fresh without the detour.

This tester pod still runs the tree-volume layout of the deployed daemon: nproc 8 and MemTotal 62 GiB with no reservation, five issue workspaces of LEGION-578 on one volume — the shape this change replaces.
